summary.en: The waistcoat of the traje de charro — the Mexican horseman's suit. Short, close, cut in worsted wool, with peaked lapels and a hook-and-bar front that closes edge to edge. Its length is set by the trouser, not by the torso.
summary.es: El chaleco del traje de charro. Corto, ceñido, cortado en lana peinada, con solapa de pico y un frente de corchete y barra que cierra a tope. Su largo lo fija el pantalón, no el torso.

sections: Why it earns its rank — and why it is not the waistcoat
The two things that must solve

era: Contemporary, in continuous use; the dress of a living regulated practice

custodians: the sastres and artisans who make the traje de charro
the families who own their greca designs and silverwork
Federación Mexicana de Charrería (competition dress codes)

note.en: Charrería is Mexico's national sport and a living practice, recognised by UNESCO in 2016 as Intangible Cultural Heritage. The traje de charro is its working and formal dress, worn by charros and charras, by mariachi musicians, and at weddings and civic occasions.
note.es: La charrería es el deporte nacional de México y una práctica viva, reconocida por la UNESCO en 2016 como Patrimonio Cultural Inmaterial. El traje de charro es su vestimenta de trabajo y de gala, y lo visten charros y charras, músicos de mariachi, y quienes acuden a bodas y actos cívicos.

excludes: No botonadura de plata: the silverwork of the gala categories is the work and the property of the artisans who make it.
No greca designs: the braid patterns themselves belong to the makers, the regions and the families whose they are. The cartridge marks placement rows and draws no pattern.
No escudo, and no association or team insignia.
No competition dress code: what may be worn in which category belongs to the Federación Mexicana de Charrería, not to a pattern generator.
sources: UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity — charrería, inscribed 2016 (as cited by the cartridge's provenance section)
